rows.evidence: Q1: Section 2 (Materials and methods) reports a two-year field experiment (2019-2020) at Shuguang Experimental Station, Hetao Irrigation District, with five mulching x irrigation treatments in randomized blocks; own measurements of soil/canopy temperature and humidity, photosynthesis, LAI, yield and economics (Figs. 2-10, Table 2).
rows.notes: The study does not test drip irrigation. Section 2.2 states explicitly that the irrigation method was border irrigation (full 500 mm vs deficit 300 mm per season), with transparent or black plastic film mulching over a flat surface. The results (Sections 3.1-3.2, Figs. 2, 4, 5) show that plastic film mulching (under border irrigation) lowered diurnal soil temperature amplitude by about 0.4-2.2 C relative to the unmulched full-irrigation control and raised canopy air relative humidity by about 4-7% over unmulched deficit irrigation, while lowering canopy air temperature. These effects are attributed to the mulch, not to drip irrigation; the comparison is mulch vs no mulch under border irrigation. Hence the study provides no own evidence on drip irrigation under plastic mulch (DIPM) as named in the passage. Technology mismatch; Q3-Q9 set to no per instructions.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The study is a primary two-year field experiment on plastic film mulching combined with full or deficit border irrigation for spring maize in the Hetao Irrigation District; it does not involve drip irrigation, so it cannot support claims attributed to drip irrigation under plastic mulch.
